## The characters' ranking

**The richest characters** (decided 19 October 2026). At the end of a game, beside the kings' standings, the characters are ranked by wealth: purse and hoard, what they hold. Back pay and debt tablets count for nothing at the end, as for the kings ("Debts are facts; repayment is a choice"), so a loan or a fee pays only once it is paid. It shows the second game played under the kings', in which every character has a victory of his own ("Stakes, not dispositions"). During play a character knows its own wealth, not the ranking. The dead are ranked below every living character, and among themselves by what they held when they died. Dying never beats surviving, however much was held, which is the price of risk ("No age in this game"). The built ranking leaves the dead out until item 11 changes it.

**Scores.** Characters rank by gold, by weight, since gold is what wealth is kept in. The lean, still open, is that goods count for nothing until sold, so a warehouse of copper is a bet against the random ending, and the omens push merchants to sell; one rule for every ranking would instead count a character's goods at reference prices, as a realm's are, and that choice stays open with the lean. Kings are settled ("The wealth of a realm"), which answers the worry that gold, now an input to almost everything, would be counted twice or reward hoarding; and since gold sent abroad, and fees paid to characters, leave the realm, darkening omens push kings neither to hoard nor to spend, but to stop paying for what will not return before the end. Item 18 tunes how much the land weighs against gold and goods, and compares win rates per power, whether Egypt spends its gold, and what the last seasons look like, so that every king has about an equal shot. When trade is built, its own balance pass checks that goods actually flow along the routes.
